title: Do We Actually Know How Magnets Work?

cues.text: In the early 1900s, physicists Niels Bohr and Hendrika Johanna van Leeuwen
cues.en: In the early 1900s, physicists Niels Bohr and Hendrika Johanna van Leeuwen
cues.zh: 20 世紀初期，物理學家尼爾斯・波耳 和亨德里卡・約翰娜・範・列文

cues.text: separately discovered something shocking.
cues.en: separately discovered something shocking.
cues.zh: 分別發現了一件令人震驚的事。

cues.text: According to every known rule of physics, magnetism was impossible.
cues.en: According to every known rule of physics, magnetism was impossible.
cues.zh: 根據當時所有已知的物理定律， 磁性根本不可能存在。

cues.text: This finding made no sense.
cues.en: This finding made no sense.
cues.zh: 這個發現完全說不通。

cues.text: Humans had relied on magnetic compasses for a thousand years,
cues.en: Humans had relied on magnetic compasses for a thousand years,
cues.zh: 人類使用磁羅盤已經有上千年的歷史，

cues.text: and anyone who had ever held two magnetized metals
cues.en: and anyone who had ever held two magnetized metals
cues.zh: 而且，只要拿過兩塊磁化金屬的人，

cues.text: could tell you that some invisible force was acting on them.
cues.en: could tell you that some invisible force was acting on them.
cues.zh: 都能感覺到有某種 看不見的力量正在作用。

cues.text: Bohr and van Leeuwen knew they were missing something—
cues.en: Bohr and van Leeuwen knew they were missing something—
cues.zh: 波耳和範・列文知道， 一定還有他們尚未掌握的東西——

cues.text: but what?
cues.en: but what?
cues.zh: 但究竟是什麼？

cues.text: By the 1920s, physicists had learned quite a bit about the fundamentals of matter.
cues.en: By the 1920s, physicists had learned quite a bit about the fundamentals of matter.
cues.zh: 到了 1920 年代，物理學家 對物質的基本組成已有相當多的瞭解。

cues.text: They knew that every material is made of atoms,
cues.en: They knew that every material is made of atoms,
cues.zh: 他們知道，每種物質都是由原子組成，

cues.text: each comprised of a nucleus containing protons and orbited by electrons.
cues.en: each comprised of a nucleus containing protons and orbited by electrons.
cues.zh: 每個原子都有一個含有質子的原子核， 周圍則有電子執行。

cues.text: They also knew that both of these particles
cues.en: They also knew that both of these particles
cues.zh: 他們也知道，這兩種粒子 都具有幾項基本性質，

cues.text: have a few fundamental properties,
cues.en: have a few fundamental properties,
cues.zh: 包括少量的質量、電荷， 以及某種程度的磁性。

cues.text: including a small amount of mass, an electrical charge,
cues.en: including a small amount of mass, an electrical charge,
cues.zh: 包括少量的質量、電荷， 以及某種程度的磁性。

cues.text: and some amount of magnetism.
cues.en: and some amount of magnetism.
cues.zh: 這些內在屬性究竟從何而來， 至今仍是個謎。

cues.text: The origin of these intrinsic properties remains an ongoing mystery.
cues.en: The origin of these intrinsic properties remains an ongoing mystery.
cues.zh: 這些內在屬性究竟從何而來， 至今仍是個謎。

cues.text: But the result is that every electron and proton is a tiny magnet
cues.en: But the result is that every electron and proton is a tiny magnet
cues.zh: 但呈現的結果是，每個電子和質子 都是一個微小的磁鐵，

cues.text: that works just like their full-size counterparts.
cues.en: that works just like their full-size counterparts.
cues.zh: 作用方式就像 我們熟悉的大型磁鐵一樣。

cues.text: Both have invisible magnetic fields that radiate out in closed loops
cues.en: Both have invisible magnetic fields that radiate out in closed loops
cues.zh: 兩者都有看不見的磁場，

cues.text: from one end to the other.
cues.en: from one end to the other.
cues.zh: 這些磁極會受到其他磁鐵 異極的密集磁力線吸引，

cues.text: These magnetic poles are attracted to the dense field lines
cues.en: These magnetic poles are attracted to the dense field lines
cues.zh: 這些磁極會受到其他磁鐵 異極的密集磁力線吸引，

cues.text: of the opposite pole of other magnets,
cues.en: of the opposite pole of other magnets,
cues.zh: 並被方向相反的磁場排斥。

cues.text: and repelled by fields flowing in the opposite direction.
cues.en: and repelled by fields flowing in the opposite direction.
cues.zh: 並被方向相反的磁場排斥。

cues.text: Of course, researchers still had questions.
cues.en: Of course, researchers still had questions.
cues.zh: 當然，研究人員還是有許多疑問。

cues.text: What determines the direction of these magnetic fields?
cues.en: What determines the direction of these magnetic fields?
cues.zh: 究竟是什麼決定了這些磁場的方向？

cues.text: And if every atom is composed of tiny magnets,
cues.en: And if every atom is composed of tiny magnets,
cues.zh: 而且，如果每個原子 都是由微小磁鐵組成的，

cues.text: why isn't everything magnetic?
cues.en: why isn't everything magnetic?
cues.zh: 為什麼不是所有東西都具有磁性？

cues.text: The answers emerged with the birth of quantum mechanics:
cues.en: The answers emerged with the birth of quantum mechanics:
cues.zh: 答案隨著量子力學的誕生而逐漸浮現。

cues.text: a new branch of physics exploring how the laws of nature work differently
cues.en: a new branch of physics exploring how the laws of nature work differently
cues.zh: 量子力學是一門新的物理學分支，

cues.text: at the sub-atomic level.
cues.en: at the sub-atomic level.
cues.zh: 1926 年，兩位荷蘭物理學家發現，

cues.text: In 1926, a pair of Dutch physicists discovered that—
cues.en: In 1926, a pair of Dutch physicists discovered that—
cues.zh: 1926 年，兩位荷蘭物理學家發現，

cues.text: in addition to mass, charge, and magnetism—
cues.en: in addition to mass, charge, and magnetism—
cues.zh: 除了質量、電荷和磁性之外，

cues.text: particles had another fundamental property:
cues.en: particles had another fundamental property:
cues.zh: 粒子還具有另一項基本特性：

cues.text: quantum spin.
cues.en: quantum spin.
cues.zh: 量子自旋。

cues.text: This is a confusing label because while nothing is actually spinning,
cues.en: This is a confusing label because while nothing is actually spinning,
cues.zh: 這個名稱很容易讓人困惑， 因為粒子其實並沒有真的在旋轉；

cues.text: spin does refer to a kind of innate direction
cues.en: spin does refer to a kind of innate direction
cues.zh: 不過，「自旋」確實代表 一種粒子與生俱來的方向性，

cues.text: that influences a particle’s behavior.
cues.en: that influences a particle’s behavior.
cues.zh: 會影響粒子的行為。

cues.text: And in the 1930s, Nobel Prize laureate John H. Van Vleck
cues.en: And in the 1930s, Nobel Prize laureate John H. Van Vleck
cues.zh: 到了 1930 年代，諾貝爾獎得主 約翰・H・範・弗萊克發現，

cues.text: discovered that this property held the answer
cues.en: discovered that this property held the answer
cues.zh: 這項特性解答了無數關於磁性的問題——

cues.text: to countless questions about magnetism—
cues.en: to countless questions about magnetism—
cues.zh: 這項特性解答了無數關於磁性的問題——

cues.text: including Bohr and van Leeuwen’s.
cues.en: including Bohr and van Leeuwen’s.
cues.zh: 包括波耳和範・列文所提出的疑問。

cues.text: Basically, the direction of a particle’s spin
cues.en: Basically, the direction of a particle’s spin
cues.zh: 簡單來說，粒子的自旋方向 決定了它的磁場方向。

cues.text: determines the direction of its magnetic field.
cues.en: determines the direction of its magnetic field.
cues.zh: 而由於電子的磁場比質子強得多，

cues.text: And since electrons have much stronger magnetic fields than protons,
cues.en: And since electrons have much stronger magnetic fields than protons,
cues.zh: 而由於電子的磁場比質子強得多，

cues.text: the direction of their spin determines whether or not something is magnetic.
cues.en: the direction of their spin determines whether or not something is magnetic.
cues.zh: 因此電子的自旋方向 就決定了某種物質是否具有磁性。

cues.text: If enough of a material's electrons spin in the same direction,
cues.en: If enough of a material's electrons spin in the same direction,
cues.zh: 如果一種材料中有足夠多的電子 朝著同一方向自旋，

cues.text: their many tiny magnetic fields will align,
cues.en: their many tiny magnetic fields will align,
cues.zh: 它們產生的眾多微小磁場就會排列整齊，

cues.text: turning the material into a magnet with a field pointing in that direction.
cues.en: turning the material into a magnet with a field pointing in that direction.
cues.zh: 使這種材料變成磁鐵，

cues.text: The more aligned electrons, the stronger the magnet.
cues.en: The more aligned electrons, the stronger the magnet.
cues.zh: 電子排列得越一致， 磁鐵的磁性就越強。

cues.text: On the other hand,
cues.en: On the other hand,
cues.zh: 反過來說，

cues.text: if a material is full of electrons with competing spins
cues.en: if a material is full of electrons with competing spins
cues.zh: 如果一種材料裡充滿 自旋方向彼此不同的電子，

cues.text: their fields cancel each other out,
cues.en: their fields cancel each other out,
cues.zh: 它們的磁場會彼此抵消，

cues.text: leaving you with something non-magnetic.
cues.en: leaving you with something non-magnetic.
cues.zh: 最後結果就是不具磁性的材料。

cues.text: Most elements have electrons that come in pairs
cues.en: Most elements have electrons that come in pairs
cues.zh: 大多數元素的電子都是成對存在，

cues.text: and spin in opposite directions,
cues.en: and spin in opposite directions,
cues.zh: 而且自旋方向相反，

cues.text: which is why most materials aren’t magnetic.
cues.en: which is why most materials aren’t magnetic.
cues.zh: 這就是為什麼大多數材料沒有磁性。

cues.text: But iron, nickel, cobalt, and a few rare metals
cues.en: But iron, nickel, cobalt, and a few rare metals
cues.zh: 但鐵、鎳、鈷， 以及少數幾種稀有金屬，

cues.text: prefer to leave some of their electrons unpaired.
cues.en: prefer to leave some of their electrons unpaired.
cues.zh: 則傾向於讓部分電子 維持不成對的狀態。

cues.text: This doesn’t automatically make them magnetic—
cues.en: This doesn’t automatically make them magnetic—
cues.zh: 這並不代表它們就一定具有磁性——

cues.text: just because their electrons are unpaired
cues.en: just because their electrons are unpaired
cues.zh: 電子沒有成對，

cues.text: doesn’t mean they always spin in the same direction.
cues.en: doesn’t mean they always spin in the same direction.
cues.zh: 並不表示它們總是朝著同一方向自旋。

cues.text: However, they can be nudged into alignment
cues.en: However, they can be nudged into alignment
cues.zh: 然而，這些電子可以透過 與鄰近原子的互動作用，

cues.text: by interacting with neighboring atoms.
cues.en: by interacting with neighboring atoms.
cues.zh: 被逐漸推向一致的方向。

cues.text: And researchers can kick-start this process
cues.en: And researchers can kick-start this process
cues.zh: 要啟動這個過程， 研究人員可以藉由施加強磁場，

cues.text: by applying a strong magnetic field
cues.en: by applying a strong magnetic field
cues.zh: 要啟動這個過程， 研究人員可以藉由施加強磁場，

cues.text: or by heating and cooling the material inside a weaker magnetic field.
cues.en: or by heating and cooling the material inside a weaker magnetic field.
cues.zh: 或是在較弱的磁場中 加熱、冷卻這些物質。

cues.text: These metals will stay magnets permanently unless their electrons are scrambled
cues.en: These metals will stay magnets permanently unless their electrons are scrambled
cues.zh: 這些金屬會永久保持磁性，

cues.text: by intense heat or an extremely strong magnetic field.
cues.en: by intense heat or an extremely strong magnetic field.
cues.zh: 除非強烈的高溫或極強的磁場 使它們的電子排列變得混亂。

cues.text: But this magnetization process can make anything magnetic temporarily.
cues.en: But this magnetization process can make anything magnetic temporarily.
cues.zh: 不過，這種磁化的過程 也能讓任何物質暫時具有磁性。

cues.text: Felix Bloch and Edward Mills Purcell took advantage of this in 1945
cues.en: Felix Bloch and Edward Mills Purcell took advantage of this in 1945
cues.zh: 1945 年，費利克斯・布洛赫 和愛德華・米爾斯・珀塞爾

cues.text: when they invented nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.
cues.en: when they invented nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.
cues.zh: 就利用了這項特性， 發展出核磁共振光譜法。

cues.text: This technology uses a strong magnetic field
cues.en: This technology uses a strong magnetic field
cues.zh: 這項技術利用強磁場，

cues.text: to temporarily align a material's protons,
cues.en: to temporarily align a material's protons,
cues.zh: 暫時讓材料中的質子排列一致，

cues.text: then a weaker field to knock specific molecules out of alignment.
cues.en: then a weaker field to knock specific molecules out of alignment.
cues.zh: 再以較弱的磁場使特定分子中的質子 偏離原本的排列。

cues.text: The machine then tracks the electromagnetic energy
cues.en: The machine then tracks the electromagnetic energy
cues.zh: 接著，儀器會追蹤這些受到擾動的質子 重新排列時所釋放的電磁能量，

cues.text: expended by the jostled protons as they realign,
cues.en: expended by the jostled protons as they realign,
cues.zh: 接著，儀器會追蹤這些受到擾動的質子 重新排列時所釋放的電磁能量，

cues.text: allowing researchers to map the material's molecular structure.
cues.en: allowing researchers to map the material's molecular structure.
cues.zh: 藉此描繪出物質的分子結構。

cues.text: This invention laid the groundwork for MRI machines,
cues.en: This invention laid the groundwork for MRI machines,
cues.zh: 這項發明為磁振造影 (MRI) 奠定了基礎。

cues.text: which use a similar approach to magnetize the water in our bodies
cues.en: which use a similar approach to magnetize the water in our bodies
cues.zh: MRI 採用類似的方法， 磁化人體內的水分子，

cues.text: and map our tissues.
cues.en: and map our tissues.
cues.zh: 進而描繪出身體組織的結構。

cues.text: Of course, NMR and MRI are just two of countless modern technologies
cues.en: Of course, NMR and MRI are just two of countless modern technologies
cues.zh: 當然，

cues.text: that rely on magnetism.
cues.en: that rely on magnetism.
cues.zh: 電腦硬碟、電動機、 揚聲器、無線通訊——

cues.text: Computer hard drives, electric motors, speakers, wireless communication—
cues.en: Computer hard drives, electric motors, speakers, wireless communication—
cues.zh: 電腦硬碟、電動機、 揚聲器、無線通訊——

cues.text: all these inventions prove that not only does magnetism exist,
cues.en: all these inventions prove that not only does magnetism exist,
cues.zh: 這些發明都證明瞭， 磁性不僅確實存在，

cues.text: but studying this phenomenon remains endlessly attractive.
cues.en: but studying this phenomenon remains endlessly attractive.
cues.zh: 這個現象的研究也始終充滿吸引力。
